transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-13
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Maria Lopez (Lighthouse - Head of Security), Daniel Kim (Eng Manager), Priya Shah (DevOps), Omar Ruiz (Product)

Summary: quick weekly POC security sync, covered SSO/SAML config, audit log formats and retention, SOC2 evidence request, KMS integration questions, and next steps for network/VPC walkthrough. Some audio dropped at ~00:22, minor transcription artifacts.

00:00:00 - Avery Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, yeah this is our weekly security sync for the lighthouse pilot, um I'll hand it to Samir to run through the Okta and SSO bits then we'll go into logs and SOC2 questions
00:00:18 - Samir Patel: cool thanks, yeah so quick reminder of where we are \u2014 pilot's in dev, traffic is small, we saw the KV cache prefix hit ratio go up after the prompt tuning, um sorry K V cache, uh so that's all looking healthy
00:00:35 - Maria Lopez: great, thanks. main things for us this week are SSO, audit logs retention, and SOC2 evidence \u2014 we also want to confirm encryption at rest keys and whether we can use our KMS
00:00:50 - Samir Patel: yep on SSO we support SAML 2.0, we've done Okta a bunch \u2014 we can provide metadata and a sample SP/IdP config. a couple caveats: for dedicated/private installs the SAML assertions can be validated internally, for hosted we support SCIM and SCIM is optional, but you can do group sync via SCIM
00:01:12 - Daniel Kim: question \u2014 for hosted, are assertion attributes encrypted in transit only or are they stored? like any PII from assertions retained in logs?
00:01:24 - Samir Patel: good q, default is we don't persist full assertion dumps; we persist an audit entry with user id, timestamp, and result (success/fail). the actual SAML assertion body isn't stored in plaintext in our long-term logs, though there may be short-lived debug traces if you enable high-verbosity logging
00:01:42 - Priya Shah: what's the retention window for those audit entries? we need 90 days at minimum per our compliance baseline
00:01:50 - Jordan Lee: right now hosted default is 30 days for high-level audit logs but we can configure up to 365 for enterprise plans or Dedicated. there's also an add-on for extended retention
00:02:05 - Maria Lopez: ok we likely need 90 then. please put that as an action item.
00:02:12 - Avery Park: noted, we'll follow up. Samir can you confirm the log schema and fields?
00:02:20 - Samir Patel: yes \u2014 i'll send the schema. it includes timestamp, user_id, route, model_id, request_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, latency_ms, outcome, and a correlation_id. note \u2014 sometimes model names are abbreviated, so the model_id may look like rwd-x or similar in some traces
00:02:44 - Omar Ruiz: also we need to see sample log lines to map into our SIEM, do you ship to syslog or do you push to S3? what's the integration point
00:02:55 - Samir Patel: we can stream logs to S3, and we also have EventBridge/CloudWatch style connectors for AWS regions. for Dedicated you can configure a forwarder into your SIEM over syslog or collector agents
00:03:10 - Maria Lopez: encryption \u2014 can we bring our own keys? KMS?
00:03:15 - Samir Patel: yes BYOK for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer a managed KMS, and we also integrate with customer KMS via a bring-your-own-key flow using envelope encryption; the HSM-backed option is available for enterprise customers
00:03:32 - Daniel Kim: what about key rotation and audit? we need key rotation logs in our audit trail
00:03:38 - Samir Patel: rotation is supported, and rotation events are surfaced in the audit log. you can also request key rotation schedules and export rotation events if you need them for your KMS audit
00:03:50 - Maria Lopez: SOC2 \u2014 we've requested the attestation, what's the turnaround?
00:03:55 - Avery Park: we will send the current SOC 2 Type II attestation and the control matrix; samir will include the list of in-scope controls and where evidence lives. expecting to share by next week
00:04:10 - Maria Lopez: perfect, we also need the evidence for encryption controls and logging controls specific to the pilot
00:04:18 - Jordan Lee: we'll include a pointer to the evidence bundle and provide guidance on how to validate. note there may be some redactions for customer data in the standard package but we can include screenshots and config extracts for the pilot
00:04:35 - Priya Shah: question on network \u2014 for the VPC peering / private deployment test, do you support single-tenant VPC peering or do we need a VPN?
00:04:45 - Samir Patel: for Private we do direct VPC peering; for Hosted we have private endpoints and the option for VPC peering in certain regions. we'll need to run a network walkthrough; there's usually one firewall rule and a small routing setup
00:05:00 - Daniel Kim: can we do a port list and CIDR ranges? that would speed the infra team's work
00:05:06 - Samir Patel: yep i'll include a network checklist and port/CIDR details in the followup
00:05:18 - Maria Lopez: another question: RBAC \u2014 can we map LDAP groups to Redwood roles? we want least privilege for our ops team
00:05:26 - Jordan Lee: yes \u2014 RBAC is role-based and you can map via SAML group claims or SCIM group sync. Custom roles are supported in Dedicated/private, hosted has a set of pre-defined roles but also supports fine-grained permissions for enterprise customers
00:05:45 - Maria Lopez: excellent. on audit log content, we need the raw payload for model inference requests redacted \u2014 can you confirm you don't store user prompts long-term?
00:05:55 - Samir Patel: we do not store user prompts in the primary long-term audit log. we keep hashed references and correlation ids. for debugging, short-term traces may contain prompt text but those are short-lived and can be disabled; for Dedicated we can configure zero-persistence for prompt text
00:06:18 - Priya Shah: um there's sometimes slippage in the transcription here, sorry if i repeat, but can you confirm deletion timelines? we need a deletion SLA for prompt data after the pilot ends
00:06:28 - Avery Park: we can commit to deletion within 30 days after pilot termination for hosted, and immediate deletion for Dedicated/private on request; we'll put that in an agreement note
00:06:40 - Maria Lopez: ok good, please note that as a must for our security sign-off
00:06:45 - Samir Patel: noted. i'll add deletion SLA to the action items.
00:06:50 - Omar Ruiz: small thing \u2014 model versioning, we want an immutable model_id so that audit traces map to exact model binaries used
00:06:57 - Samir Patel: yes model versions are immutable in the trace and we include model hash and runtime config in the trace metadata for Dedicated; hosted includes model version id, but we can export additional metadata if you need the runtime hash
00:07:15 - Daniel Kim: any limitations on token-level billing visibility? we need per-request token counts to do cost reconciliation
00:07:23 - Jordan Lee: we provide token-level breakdowns per request in the console and can stream them to your billing export S3 bucket daily; there's also a per-route breakdown in the dashboard
00:07:36 - Maria Lopez: ok that covers most of our items. next \u2014 audit log format example would be helpful
00:07:42 - Samir Patel: i'll paste example lines in the follow-up but quick sample: {timestamp: "2026-05-13T14:59:12Z", user_id: "alice@lf.com", route: "/v1/generate", model_id: "rwd-7b-v2", request_tokens: 120, response_tokens: 640, latency_ms: 210, outcome: "success", correlation_id: "abc-123"} \u2014 note that's a simplified view, actual schema is json-lines newline separated in S3
00:08:10 - Maria Lopez: thanks. any blockers on our side to enable extended log retention?
00:08:16 - Samir Patel: just contract + billing for the retention add-on for hosted; for Dedicated it's config. so procurement/signature is the typical blocker
00:08:27 - Maria Lopez: procurement is... well, procurement. we'll start the paperwork once SOC2 docs are in hand
00:08:34 - Avery Park: understood. Samir, can you cover any outstanding security scans or penetration testing evidence?
00:08:40 - Samir Patel: we run internal pentests quarterly and use a third-party firm annually; we can share summary reports and remediation status. the raw vuln details are in our internal tracker but we'll provide sanitized summaries for the pilot
00:08:58 - Priya Shah: will the sanitized reports show CVE ids and patch versions? we need enough to validate no critical findings are outstanding
00:09:06 - Samir Patel: yes we'll include CVE ids and patch status, not necessarily the full hostnames.
00:09:15 - Maria Lopez: excellent. any public disclosures or past incidents we should be aware of?
00:09:21 - Jordan Lee: none in the past 24 months; we have routine incident reports \u2014 we'll include the timeline doc in the evidence bundle
00:09:31 - Daniel Kim: small ops note \u2014 we want to test replay of audit logs into our SIEM, is there a replay API or do you push a bulk export?
00:09:40 - Samir Patel: we can do bulk exports to S3 and you can pull; for Dedicated we can provide a replay endpoint into your account for direct ingestion
00:09:53 - Maria Lopez: ok that works.
00:10:00 - Omar Ruiz: are there any cross-tenant leakage protections for hosted in multi-tenant mode? we've seen noisy neighbor concerns
00:10:08 - Samir Patel: yes isolation is enforced by request routing and per-tenant namespaces; logical separation is strong but Dedicated gives physical separation if you need it. we also do periodic tenancy fuzz tests
00:10:22 - Maria Lopez: perfect.
00:10:26 - Avery Park: let's do a quick recap and then open the floor to anything else \u2014 recap: 1) Samir to send Okta SAML guide + sample metadata, 2) Avery to send SOC2 and controls, 3) Samir to share log schema and sample lines, 4) Samir to include deletion SLA language, 5) network checklist to be shared, 6) customer to confirm retention days
00:10:50 - Maria Lopez: sounds good. one more: do you support SSO session duration controls? we need sessions to expire at 1 hour by default
00:10:58 - Samir Patel: yes session timeout configurable via SAML assertion and our session policy; for hosted we can enforce shorter session durations for enterprise tenants
00:11:12 - Priya Shah: ok thanks.
00:11:15 - Jordan Lee: we'll schedule the network walkthrough; i'll send a calendar invite for the week of 2026-05-25.
00:11:24 - Maria Lopez: thanks everyone.
00:11:30 - Avery Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs.
00:11:34 - (audio glitch)
00:22:10 - [Transcript drop, ~20 seconds of audio lost: brief silence and reconnection]
00:22:30 - Daniel Kim: sorry i think i missed a bit \u2014 quick question: for the audit logs if we want to redact user identifiers at ingest, is that supported?
00:22:38 - Samir Patel: yes you can configure a transform pipeline to hash or redact at ingest and then store pseudonymized ids; note that will impact your correlation unless you maintain a mapping in your sidecar system
00:22:55 - Maria Lopez: ok good.
00:23:05 - Priya Shah: last compliance ask \u2014 do you provide evidence for data residency for EU tenants? we may need logs to remain in eu-west-1 region
00:23:15 - Samir Patel: yes we offer region-based tenancy and can ensure logs and compute stay in eu-west-1; that'll require a region pinning request and might affect latency/cost, we'll document tradeoffs
00:23:28 - Maria Lopez: great.
00:23:35 - Avery Park: any final blockers from lighthouse side?
00:23:40 - Maria Lopez: none immediate; getting SOC2 bundle will unblock procurement and retention confirmation will unblock infra work
00:23:49 - Avery Park: excellent, we'll push those items. thanks everyone, meeting over.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors (e.g., K V cache spacing, missing punctuation). Speakers occasionally overlap; some speaker labels are paraphrased for clarity.
file_notes: This is a routine weekly POC security sync for the Lighthouse Financial pilot. Contains action items and next steps for SOC2 documents, SSO/SAML, audit logs, retention, KMS BYOK, and network/VPC walkthrough.
